reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Structures research-funding proposals around opportunity requirements, review criteria, aims, methods, impact, schedules, budgets, supporting documents, and review cycles.
neutralIntentExamples: draft a research proposal aligned to a specified funding opportunity
revise a grant narrative and budget after reviewer feedback
prepare a milestone plan and supporting sections for a collaborative application
inputs: research goals, methods, preliminary evidence, team roles, and institutional context
budget constraints, deadlines, and reviewer feedback
operations: map proposal sections to stated evaluation criteria
draft and revise aims, significance, innovation, approach, impact, timeline, and budget justification
assemble a submission-readiness checklist and identify evidence gaps
failureBehavior: flag missing or uncertain solicitation requirements
avoid asserting current agency rules without verification
surface infeasible scope, weak evidence, misaligned budget, or missing sections for human resolution
exclusions: does not guarantee funding or reviewer approval
does not replace institutional authorization or expert scientific review
does not submit materials or transmit sensitive research data without explicit authorization
does not treat optional figure generation as mandatory
usefulInvariants: claims and proposed methods remain traceable to the supplied research plan
budget and timeline must support the stated work
agency-specific requirements must be checked against the active solicitation
figures support rather than substitute for clear aims and methods
materialRisks: agency rules, page limits, and program priorities can become stale
unpublished or sensitive details could be exposed through optional third-party figure generation
persuasive framing can overstate feasibility, impact, or preliminary evidence
submission preparation may create durable records or external commitments

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Provides a visual-design pattern library for polished web surfaces, covering layout composition, responsive collapse, layered containers, interaction motion, and rendering-performance constraints.
neutralIntentExamples: design a responsive landing page with a deliberate visual system
specify motion and interaction patterns for a polished product interface
review a web layout for responsive behavior and animation performance
inputs: available fonts, icons, images, and motion libraries
operations: select a visual and layout composition
compose layered cards, responsive sections, navigation, calls to action, and entry states
check animation properties, mobile fallback, blur usage, and stacking discipline
failureBehavior: defer unsupported assets or libraries rather than assuming availability
reduce effects for constrained, regulated, or low-performance surfaces
require separate accessibility and production-quality review
exclusions: does not establish brand strategy, conversion research, accessibility compliance, or production QA
does not require a particular framework or vendor library
does not justify decorative motion when it harms usability or performance
usefulInvariants: small-screen layouts must remain usable and avoid touch-target conflicts
animation should prefer transform and opacity over layout-triggering properties
blur and noise treatments must be bounded to appropriate layers
visual decisions must be validated against available project assets
materialRisks: prescriptive aesthetic bans can conflict with an existing design system
heavy blur, motion, and texture can impair accessibility and mobile performance
assumed premium assets may be absent or incorrectly licensed
visual novelty rules can reduce consistency across a product

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Offers the same core interface-art-direction patterns as a product-design bundle, including responsive composition, nested surfaces, interactive motion, and guardrails for rendering cost.
neutralIntentExamples: shape a product page with layered surfaces and responsive composition
define an animated navigation and call-to-action interaction model
adapt a visually rich interface for small screens and constrained devices
operations: choose a visual texture and layout arrangement
define nested containers, calls to action, navigation transitions, and viewport-entry motion
audit responsive collapse and GPU-sensitive effects
failureBehavior: scale back effects when device or product constraints require it
send accessibility, brand, and QA questions to dedicated review
exclusions: does not replace accessibility validation, brand strategy, conversion research, or production QA
does not imply that the bundled packaging is technically distinct from the companion design source
does not mandate luxury styling for every product context
usefulInvariants: responsive behavior must preserve usable controls and content hierarchy
effects should avoid animating layout dimensions
fixed-layer treatments must not become expensive scrolling effects
design guidance remains subordinate to project constraints and existing systems
materialRisks: near-duplicate source packaging can create redundant capability clusters
strong aesthetic prescriptions may produce inconsistency or exclusionary defaults
motion and backdrop effects can create accessibility and performance regressions
asset assumptions may cause implementation or licensing failures

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Describes .NET client workflows for address and coordinate lookup, routing, map imagery, IP region lookup, weather retrieval, and managed map-account access.
neutralIntentExamples: find coordinates and a normalized address for a supplied place
calculate directions or travel-time matrices between locations
retrieve a map image, reachable-area polygon, or weather conditions for a coordinate
inputs: addresses, coordinates, IP addresses, route points, and query options
requested imagery, routing, weather, batch, and regional parameters
operations: call search, reverse search, boundary, routing, rendering, geolocation, and weather endpoints
handle batches, asynchronous route matrices, rate limits, and service errors
optionally create or retrieve account SAS material
outputs: routes, durations, matrices, and reachable polygons
country or region, weather conditions, and alerts
provider error status and diagnostic information
failureBehavior: surface authentication, invalid-parameter, rate-limit, and service failures
use bounded retry and backoff for rate limiting
avoid persisting map imagery or credentials unless explicitly required and authorized
treat preview SDK versions and documented limits as verification points
exclusions: does not make location data accurate, current, or suitable for safety-critical decisions by itself
does not authorize access to another account or disclose subscription keys
does not guarantee current package versions, quotas, pricing, or API behavior
does not imply that account management or SAS creation is needed for ordinary lookup
usefulInvariants: credentials must be supplied through protected configuration and never emitted in output
longitude and latitude ordering must be preserved
batch and matrix limits must be respected
external calls and durable file writes require explicit scope and authorization
provider documentation must be checked before relying on prerelease APIs
materialRisks: location and IP data are sensitive and can enable tracking or inference
subscription keys and SAS tokens can grant billable or privileged access
network calls can incur cost, rate limits, and provider-side logging
sample code writes files and account workflows can mutate cloud resources
stated preview versions and limits may be stale
